transcript:
Header: 2027-03-09 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Alex Martin (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Rodriguez (Redwood SE), Dana Lee (Quasar Head of ML), Miguel Santos (Platform Eng), Rina Patel (SRE), Omar Khan (Product)

Summary (auto): Quick intro, then deep dive on reliability and incident tolerance. Quasar is evaluating whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private fits their PCI-adjacent fraud detection workload; big concerns are multi-region failover, clear SLAs, and data residency.

00:00:08 - Alex Martin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood — I'll kick us off. Um, quick round-robin?
00:00:18 - Dana Lee: Hi all, Dana here, head of ML at Quasar, we're evaluating LLM infra for a fraud screen project.
00:00:25 - Miguel Santos: Miguel, platform eng, I'll own the integration work.
00:00:29 - Rina Patel: Rina, SRE, I'll focus on reliability and compliance.
00:00:34 - Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood SE, I'll cover technical details on routing and fallbacks.
00:00:40 - Alex Martin: Great, goal for today is to understand your failure modes and SLOs so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and a fallback strategy.

00:02:05 - Dana Lee: High level — the fraud model needs near real-time scoring for charge approvals. p50 is 120ms for a single model call, p95 we target under 400ms. Throughput around 120 req/s peak, but can spike up to 500 req/s during promos. Data is PCI-adjacent, so we have to keep PII encrypted and EU residency is preferred.

00:03:12 - Priya Nair: Got it. Two quick clarifying Qs — do you need model training in your environment? And do you require the inference instances to be in a private VPC?
00:03:21 - Dana Lee: Training stays internal. For inference we'd prefer VPC or Dedicated, but open to Hosted if we can get a VPC peering and strict KMS control.

00:04:40 - Rina Patel: For SRE — our ask is that when a region degrades, traffic should automatically fail over to another region within 30s, with clear SLAs on request success and fallbacks to a cheaper model if the primary is down. Also audit logs for every request.

00:05:12 - Priya Nair: Perfect — Redwood supports multi-region routing and model fallbacks. Two patterns: 1) Active-active multi-region with smart routing at the control plane, and 2) Active-primary with automatic fallback to a secondary region. In practice, failover times depend on DNS and health checks, but with our routing policy you can get sub-30s failover plus a soft-fallback to a smaller quantized model to keep throughput.

00:06:30 - Miguel Santos: When you say "soft-fallback" what changes? Latency? Token cost?
00:06:36 - Priya Nair: Soft-fallback means the runtime will switch to a compatible, lower-cost/quantized variant — typically a small hit on output quality and lower per-token GPU time, but it keeps latency stable and avoids request failures. We also have forced fallback policies that switch to a cached response or stub output for non-critical paths.

00:07:50 - Alex Martin: On SLAs — our Dedicated customers get a 99.9% uptime SLA for the provisioned pool and latency SLOs per model type. Hosted customers have a best-effort latency but still get availability metrics and per-token cost. Private deployments can have custom SLAs negotiated.

00:08:40 - Dana Lee: We need a written SLA for availability and end-to-end success rate for fraud calls — regulatory will want that. Does Redwood provide an error budget and rollbacks for deploy regressions?
00:08:56 - Sam Rodriguez: Yes, we expose error budgets and rollout controls in Console — canaries, automatic rollback on error-rate spikes, and tie-in to quality monitoring so you can block a rollout if evals regress.

00:10:15 - Rina Patel: For multi-region, how do you handle consistency for cached KV? Our fraud model uses a short-term user KV cache to accelerate scoring — if we failover to another region we must not serve stale KV that causes incorrect scoring.
00:10:35 - Priya Nair: Great question. We have two approaches: global prefix cache with TTLs and cross-region replication for critical keys, or stateless inference with an external store. For heavy consistency needs we recommend Dedicated with a regional cross-replication plan, or Private where you control the KV store replication. Global cache replication usually has eventual consistency — so we'd tune TTLs and accept small windows, or we sync keys on failover for critical flows.

00:12:02 - Miguel Santos: Any example numbers on failover latency and increased p95 after failover?
00:12:10 - Priya Nair: In our benchmarks, active-active failover with smart routing adds ~50-150ms for the first few requests while caches warm up; p95 can spike 2x for a few minutes depending on model warming and cold start. With continuous KV caching and pre-warmed replicas on Dedicated, that spike can be <20%.

00:13:45 - Dana Lee: What about cost implications — running active-active across two regions sounds expensive.
00:13:52 - Alex Martin: Correct — active-active double-runs capacity. For cost-sensitive teams we recommend active-primary with warm standby in the secondary region and automated promotion on health checks. You pay for minimal reserved capacity in the standby region. We can show cost models comparing (A) single region with aggressive fallback models, (B) active-primary with warm standby, (C) active-active.

00:15:05 - Omar Khan: On the legal side, we need audit logs for every request and key access logs. KMS must be customer-managed and HSM if possible. Is that supported?
00:15:18 - Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS. For Hosted we support Bring-Your-Own-KMS via our private tenancy options; HSM integrations are available for Private deployments. All modes support detailed request audit logs and admin activity logs.

00:16:40 - Rina Patel: How do you handle partial degradation like GPU OOMs causing increased latency but not outright failures? Do you route around those nodes quickly?
00:16:51 - Sam Rodriguez: Our runtime monitors per-node health (latency, queue length, OOMs) and automatically routes away from degraded nodes. For Dedicated you can set autoscaling and node retirement policies. In severe cases we can fallback to a smaller quantized model or queue with backpressure and return a 202-type response recommending retry.

00:18:12 - Miguel Santos: During DR drills we want predictable behavior — can we run simulated failovers?
00:18:20 - Priya Nair: Absolutely — we can run fault-injection drills in Dedicated or Private. For Hosted customers we provide a staging environment and a guided playbook for injection testing. We'll share a runbook.

00:19:40 - Dana Lee: Any regulatory concerns for EU data residency if traffic fails over to a US region?
00:19:50 - Priya Nair: We can enforce routing policies by customer region — block failover to non-EU regions unless explicitly allowed. For strict EU residency you would choose Dedicated in EU-only regions or Private on-prem.

00:20:58 - Omar Khan: If we pick Dedicated, what's the typical lead time for provisioning a multi-region pool?
00:21:05 - Alex Martin: Typical is 2–4 weeks depending on region and sizing; for Private it can be longer (4–8 weeks). Hosted is immediate for basic access but VPC peering and BYOK may add several days.

00:22:15 - Miguel Santos: On telemetry — can we get per-request tracing to our tracing system?
00:22:22 - Sam Rodriguez: Yes, we have tracing hooks and exporters for Jaeger/Zipkin/OTel, and you can push traces and token-level cost metadata into your observability stack.

00:23:40 - Dana Lee: Let's talk about fallback policy specifics — we need: (a) fallback to quantized model preserving latency, (b) fallback to cached response for low-priority flows, (c) circuit-breaker that returns safe default when error rate crosses threshold. Can Redwood express all three?
00:24:00 - Priya Nair: Yes — policies are declarative in the Console. You can define priorities per route: e.g., primary model -> fallback model A -> cached response -> stub. Circuit-breakers, retry budgets, and per-route thresholds are supported. And you can tie policies to customer tiers or routes.

00:25:33 - Rina Patel: We also need the ability to audit when a fallback happened and why — minutes, stack trace, affected requests.
00:25:41 - Priya Nair: Every fallback event is logged with reason codes and request IDs; we'll expose a queryable dashboard and raw logs for export.

00:26:55 - Dana Lee: For our pilots we'd like to run a PoC that simulates region outage and measure end-to-end fraud decision correctness. What would you recommend?
00:27:06 - Alex Martin: Start with a Hosted pilot to validate integration and routing policies, then run a Dedicated pilot for production-like failover and KV replication testing. We'll provide a benchmark sheet and a test harness.

00:28:30 - Miguel Santos: Any gotchas on data retention and logs? We need logs for 12 months, but don't want to keep PII in logs.

00:28:40 - Priya Nair: We support configurable log retention and PII redaction at ingestion. For Dedicated/Private you control retention and export; for Hosted we offer retention tiers and redaction rules.

00:30:02 - Dana Lee: Can you share SOC 2 and encryption docs today?
00:30:08 - Alex Martin: We'll email the certs and a security pack — Priya will point you at the runbook and KMS integration docs.

00:31:20 - Rina Patel: One more question on routing — do you do client-side routing or a control-plane-level routing? Our clients are internal microservices in k8s clusters across regions.
00:31:31 - Priya Nair: We do control-plane routing. You point at per-region endpoints and our control plane decides route per policy. For very low-latency scenarios we can provide region-local endpoints and SDK routing hints.

00:33:00 - Omar Khan: From a procurement perspective, we need a clear price for Dedicated with warm standby. Also draft terms for data residency and incident response in the contract.
00:33:12 - Alex Martin: We'll draft a pricing scenario and sample terms. Procurement usually sees a one-page SOW for Dedicated plus standard contract addendum for data residency.

00:34:40 - Dana Lee: What about model version pinning and rollbacks? We need to be able to pin to a model for a route and lock rollouts until manual approval.
00:34:50 - Sam Rodriguez: Supported — per-route model pins, canary percentages, and manual gates. Also automatic rollback on regression.

00:36:05 - Miguel Santos: Do you have examples of customers who did multi-region Dedicated for latency-sensitive workloads?
00:36:10 - Priya Nair: Yes, a payments customer did active-primary with warm standby and reduced failover p95 to <30% increase; we can share an anonymized case study.

00:37:30 - Dana Lee: Risk: if fallback model produces a false negative for fraud, that could be costly. How do you suggest we balance this?
00:37:40 - Alex Martin: Two levers — route critical scoring to Dedicated with stricter fallbacks (e.g., on fallback escalate to human review rather than auto-approve), and build ensemble checks where a cheap fast model triggers a secondary async check. We can help tune thresholds in Redwood Optimize.

00:39:05 - Priya Nair: For your pilot, we'll propose a fallback policy that fails safe (i.e., for high-risk routes return "flag for review" instead of allow) and a secondary async verification path.

00:40:20 - Miguel Santos: Timing — if we start next week, how soon can we run a Hosted pilot?
00:40:26 - Alex Martin: Hosted pilot can start in 2–3 days after NDA and test data. Dedicated pilot planning takes 1–2 weeks.

00:41:15 - Dana Lee: Great. Also please include an ops playbook for DR drills.
00:41:20 - Priya Nair: We'll include a playbook and a sample fault-injection checklist.

00:42:30 - Alex Martin: Do a quick recap: we'll send pricing and fallback config, security pack, and schedule POC planning. Any other asks?
00:42:42 - Rina Patel: Please include KMS BYOK steps and HSM options in the security pack.
00:42:50 - Dana Lee: Include the benchmark spreadsheet template.
00:43:00 - Alex Martin: Noted. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with next steps.

00:47:20 - (call ends)

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hears (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes as "K V cache"). References: shared deck (link provided in chat), benchmark spreadsheet (redwood.com/pilot/benchmarks), SOC2 cert (redwood.com/security/soc2).
notes: Customer leans Dedicated for critical fraud scoring but wants to validate Hosted pilot first. Main blockers: legal/contract for EU residency and KMS control. Agreed next steps and owners.
